title: Weekend Plans
summary: Two friends talk about their weekend plans: visiting a museum, watching a film, and meeting for coffee.
description: A friendly elementary dialogue about free-time activities. The dialogue recycles the present continuous for plans (I'm going to / We're meeting) and time expressions for the weekend.

vocabulary.definition: having no work or plans; available
a friendly way to say 'that is a good idea'
used to show that something is possible but not certain
to come together at the same place, usually socially

dialogue.text: Hi, Sara. What are you doing this weekend?
Not much. On Saturday morning, I am going to the museum with my brother.
That sounds nice. Are you going to the new photography exhibition?
Yes, exactly. And in the evening, I am watching a film at home.
On Sunday, I am free in the afternoon. Do you want to meet up?
Sure. We can have coffee around three.
Perfect. I will see you at the café on Sunday at three.

questions.q: What is Sara doing on Saturday morning?
When do the friends plan to meet?
What are they going to do together?

trueFalse.statement: Sara is going to the museum with her sister.
trueFalse.explanation: Sara says she is going with her brother.

trueFalse.statement: They agree to meet at three o'clock.
trueFalse.explanation: Speaker 1 says 'We can have coffee around three.'

teacherTips: Recycle the present continuous for plans. After listening, ask 'What are you doing this weekend?' around the class.
Practise the expression 'sounds good / sounds nice / sounds relaxing' as natural responses to plans.
Extension: students write three sentences about their own weekend using 'I'm going to…' and share in pairs.

es.title: Planes de fin de semana
es.summary: Dos amigos hablan de sus planes para el fin de semana: visitar un museo, ver una película y quedar para tomar un café.
es.description: Un diálogo elemental amable sobre actividades de tiempo libre. El diálogo recicla el presente continuo para planes (I'm going to / We're meeting) y expresiones de tiempo para el fin de semana.
es.topicName: Fin de semana y tiempo libre

vocabulary.definition: una forma amable de decir 'es una buena idea'
se usa para mostrar que algo es posible pero no seguro
reunirse en el mismo lugar, normalmente en un contexto social

questions.q: ¿Qué hace Sara el sábado por la mañana?

trueFalse.statement: Sara va al museo con su hermana.
trueFalse.explanation: Sara dice que va con su hermano.
El interlocutor 1 dice 'We can have coffee around three'.

teacherTips: Recicla el presente continuo para planes. Después de escuchar, pregunta 'What are you doing this weekend?' por la clase.
Practica la expresión 'sounds good / sounds nice / sounds relaxing' como respuestas naturales a planes.
Ampliación: los estudiantes escriben tres frases sobre su propio fin de semana usando 'I'm going to…' y las comparten por parejas.
